sub: Named after aṭ-Ṭūr, “the Mount”, the first oath in ayah 1
theme: Allah swears the punishment will surely come, shows the fate of the deniers and the joy of the righteous, then answers the Quraysh’s insults one question at a time. The Prophet ﷺ is told to be patient.
story: Revealed in Makkah, in the same period as adh-Dhāriyāt. The Prophet ﷺ was facing a storm of objections and accusations, though severe persecution had not yet begun.
The Quraysh chiefs called him a sorcerer, a madman and a poet, said he invented the Qurʾān, wished death on him, and plotted to end his mission. They told people not to take him seriously.
The surah is the reply: the Hereafter is certain, both its outcomes are shown, and every objection is met with a question. The Prophet ﷺ is told to keep going, be patient, and glorify his Lord.

sections.title: Oaths by Ṭūr, Book, House, sky and sea: punishment will surely fall
sections.meaning: Allah swears by five great things: Mount Ṭūr, a written Book on open parchment, the Frequented House, the raised roof of the sky, and the sea set ablaze or kept full. The point of all these oaths: your Lord’s punishment will certainly happen, and nothing can push it back.
points: By Mount Ṭūr
By a Book written on open parchment
By the Frequented House
By the sky’s raised roof, and the sea ablaze or full
Your Lord’s punishment will fall; nothing can stop it
sections.matters: Every oath points to the same answer in ayah 7: the punishment is real and unstoppable. The rest of the surah builds on it: what that Day looks like, who is saved, and why the deniers have no excuse.
sections.story: No specific incident. ʿUmar reportedly heard a man reciting up to ayat 7–8, said “By the Lord of the Kaʿbah, a true oath,” and fell ill for weeks. In one report, these ayat moved Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim to accept Islam.
explained: Ṭūr is the mountain where Allah spoke to Mūsā. The kitāb masṭūr is either the Preserved Tablet, a revealed scripture, or each person’s record of deeds. Al-bayt al-maʿmūr is the House above the seventh heaven, visited every day by seventy thousand angels who never return; or it is the Kaʿbah, always full of worshippers.

As-saqf al-marfūʿ is the sky, a roof over creation. Al-baḥr al-masjūr is either the sea that will be set ablaze on the Last Day, or the sea kept full and held back from flooding the land. All of these swear to one fact: the punishment will land, and nothing can repel it.
teaches: Allah’s warning comes with an oath; treat it as certain.
No one can push back the punishment of Allah.
Creation and revelation both point to the Hereafter.
Let the Qurʾān move your heart, as it moved ʿUmar.
sections.hook: Ayat 1–6 open with wa- (except 3), and 2–6 all end on the same ma-ū- shape: masṭūr, manshūr, maʿmūr, marfūʿ, masjūr. Ayat 7–8 answer: wāqiʿ, dāfiʿ.

sections.title: Sky sways, mountains move: deniers are shoved into the Fire they denied
sections.meaning: The punishment comes on the Day the sky sways and the mountains move away. Woe to the deniers who spent life playing in falsehood. They are shoved into Hell and told: this is the Fire you denied. Is it magic? Enter it. Patience or panic, it makes no difference.
points: The sky sways violently; the mountains move away
Woe to the deniers, busy playing in falsehood
Shoved into Hell: “This is the Fire you denied”
“Is this magic, or can you not see?”
Burn in it; patience or not, it’s all the same
sections.matters: Section 1 swore the punishment will come. This section shows when and to whom: on the Last Day, to the deniers. Their charge in this world was “magic”; in the Fire that same word is thrown back at them.
sections.story: No specific incident. The deniers used to call the Prophet ﷺ’s message magic, so in the Fire they are asked whether this, too, is magic.
explained: On that Day the sky tamūr: it heaves, spins and shakes. The mountains leave their places and become scattered dust. If such huge things are shaken, imagine a weak human. Wayl, every kind of misery, is for the deniers who lived in khawḍ: plunging into falsehood and treating the religion as a game.

They are dragged and shoved into Hell. The keepers say: this is the Fire you called a lie. You called the message magic; is this magic too, or were you blind? Enter it. Enduring it or crying out changes nothing. This is simply the result of what you did.
teaches: Treating the religion as a game has a real price.
What people mock now, they will one day see with their own eyes.
Patience helps in this life; in the Fire it changes nothing.
Allah wrongs no one: each gets what they did.
sections.hook: Three verbs repeat as nouns: tamūru mawrā (9), tasīru sayrā (10), yudaʿʿūna daʿʿā (13). Ayat 14 and 16 both use kuntum: “you used to deny”, “you used to do”. Page 524 starts at ayah 15.

sections.title: The righteous feast in gardens, their children joined, recalling their fear
sections.meaning: In contrast, the righteous are in gardens, saved from the Fire, eating and drinking in joy, reclining on lined-up couches, married to ḥūr. Their believing children are raised to their level with no loss to anyone. They turn to each other and recall: we feared Allah and called on Him, and He saved us.
points: The righteous in gardens, enjoying His gifts, saved from the Fire
Eat and drink happily; couches in rows, spouses with beautiful eyes
Believing children joined to them; each person held by his deeds
Fruit, meat, a cup with no foul talk, servants like pearls
They ask each other: we were fearful among our families
We used to call on Him; He is al-Barr, ar-Raḥīm
sections.matters: The surah holds warning and hope together: right after the Fire comes Paradise. It gives a rare comfort, that believing families are reunited, while making clear no one carries another’s sins. And it shows the path there: fear of Allah at home, and constant duʿāʾ.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Prophet ﷺ reportedly said Allah raises a believer’s children to his rank in Paradise, even if their deeds fell short, to delight him, and then recited ayah 21.
explained: The righteous are in gardens, delighted with their Lord’s gifts and saved from the Fire. They eat and drink happily, recline on couches in rows, and are married to ḥūr ʿīn. Their children who followed them in faith are raised to their rank, and the parents lose nothing. Yet each person is pledged to his own deeds.

Fruit and meat keep coming, whatever they crave. A cup passes between them with no idle or sinful talk, and servants like hidden pearls attend them. They turn to one another and recall: we were afraid among our families, so Allah favoured us and saved us. We used to call on Him; He is al-Barr, ar-Raḥīm.
teaches: Fear of Allah in this life brings safety in the next.
Raise your children on faith; Allah may join them to your rank.
No one is punished for another person’s sins.
Keep making duʿāʾ; the people of Paradise name it as their way there.
Paradise’s pleasures come without the harms of this world’s.
sections.hook: Ayah 19 ends with kuntum taʿmalūn, just like ayah 16: same words, Fire then Paradise. The ۞ falls at ayah 24. Ayat 26 and 28 both say innā kunnā, “we used to”.

sections.title: Keep reminding: not soothsayer, madman or poet; let them match the Qurʾān
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ is told to keep reminding. By Allah’s grace he is no soothsayer or madman. They call him a poet and await his death; he replies: wait, I am waiting too. Is this their reason, or their rebellion? They say he invented it. Then let them produce something like it.
points: So remind: you are no soothsayer and no madman
“A poet; we’ll wait for his death.” Say: wait, I wait too
Do their minds order this, or are they rebels?
“He made it up”? Then let them bring a speech like it
sections.matters: It opens the second half of the surah, turning from the Hereafter to the Quraysh’s attacks on the Prophet ﷺ. Each insult is answered, and the section ends with a challenge they could never meet: produce something like the Qurʾān.
sections.story: Reportedly the Quraysh met in Dār an-Nadwah, and one said: chain him and wait; death will take him like the poets Zuhayr and an-Nābighah. Ayah 30 answered them. In another report, they hoped he would die young like his father.
explained: Fa-dhakkir: keep reminding, and don’t stop because of what they say. By your Lord’s favour you are no kāhin, a soothsayer fed scraps of news by jinn, and no majnūn. They call you a poet and wait for rayb al-manūn, the blows of time, to finish you. Say: wait, and I will wait with you.

Do their famous minds really tell them to call the wisest man mad and the truth a lie? No, they are a people who transgress. They claim he invented it. The truth is they refuse to believe. If they mean it, let them, masters of Arabic, produce a speech like it.
teaches: Keep calling to the truth even when you are insulted.
When people have no argument, they attack the person instead.
Don’t be shaken by those waiting for you to fail.
The Qurʾān’s challenge stands: no one can produce its like.
sections.hook: Am yaqūlūna (“or do they say”) opens ayah 30 and again ayah 33. Each claim gets a reply: qul tarabbaṣū (31), bal lā yuʾminūn (33), fal-yaʾtū (34). Page 525 starts at ayah 32.

sections.title: Questions pile up: self-created? Own His treasures? Hear the unseen? Another god?
sections.meaning: Question after question: were they created from nothing, or did they create themselves? Did they create the heavens and earth? Do they hold Allah’s treasures, climb up to hear heaven, know the unseen? Daughters for Him, sons for them? Does he charge them? Do they plot? Is there another god? Glory be to Allah.
points: Created by nothing, or self-created? Did they make heaven and earth?
Do they own His treasures, or have a ladder to listen in?
Daughters for Him, sons for you? Does he ask you for payment?
Do they hold the unseen, or plan a plot? It will backfire
Another god besides Allah? Glory be to Allah above their partners
sections.matters: This is the surah’s argument for tawḥīd. Each question has only one honest answer, and every answer leads back to Allah as the Creator and the only one worthy of worship. The same questions once shook a listening disbeliever to the core.
sections.story: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim came to Madinah, still a disbeliever, about the captives of Badr. He heard the Prophet ﷺ recite aṭ-Ṭūr in Maghrib, and at ayat 35–37 said: “I felt my heart would fly away.” It helped lead him to Islam.
explained: Were they created by nothing, or did they create themselves? Both are impossible, so Allah made them, and He alone deserves worship. They didn’t create the heavens and earth either; they just lack certainty. Do they hold His treasures, deciding who gets prophethood? Do they have a ladder to heaven to eavesdrop? Then let their listener bring clear proof.

They give Allah daughters and keep sons for themselves. The Prophet ﷺ asks no fee that could weigh them down. They have no knowledge of the unseen to write from. If they plot against him, the plot falls back on them. Is there any god besides Allah? Subḥān Allāh, far above what they associate with Him.
teaches: Your own existence proves you have a Creator.
Knowing Allah is the Creator should lead to worshipping Him alone.
A caller to Allah asks people for nothing in return.
Plots against the truth end up harming the plotters.
Only Allah knows the unseen and holds the treasures.
sections.hook: Every ayah from 35 to 43 opens with am (“or”). Watch the pairs: am ʿindahum (37, 41), am lahum (38, 43). Counting from ayah 30, am appears 15 times.

sections.title: A falling sky wouldn’t convince them; leave them, be patient, glorify Allah
sections.meaning: They are so stubborn that if a piece of the sky fell on them, they would call it heaped clouds. So leave them until their Day, when their plotting is useless and no one helps them. A punishment comes even before that. Be patient: you are under Our eyes. Glorify your Lord day and night.
points: A piece of sky falling? They’d say: “Piled-up clouds”
Leave them till their Day; their plots won’t help them
A punishment before that, but most don’t know
Be patient, you’re under Our eyes; glorify Him when you rise
Glorify Him at night and as the stars fade
sections.matters: The surah ends the way its second half began, with instructions to the Prophet ﷺ: keep going, be patient, and draw strength from glorifying Allah. It also comforts him: he is never alone, but always under Allah’s watchful care.
sections.story: It answers their demand, “Make a piece of the sky fall on us.” The Prophet ﷺ was grieved by their hostility, and ayah 48 reassured him that he was under Allah’s eyes and protection.
explained: They demanded that a piece of the sky fall on them. Even if it did, they’d say: just piled-up clouds. So leave them until their Day, when they are struck down. Their plots won’t help them, and no one will save them. Before that, the wrongdoers face punishment in this world or the grave, though most don’t realise it.

Be patient with your Lord’s decision, for you are bi-aʿyuninā, under Our eyes: seen and protected. Glorify your Lord with praise when you stand, whether rising from sleep, starting prayer or leaving a gathering. Glorify Him in the night too, and at idbār an-nujūm, as the stars fade before dawn.
teaches: Stubborn hearts explain away even the clearest signs.
Hardship in this world can be a warning to turn back.
When people oppose you, remember Allah sees and protects you.
Draw patience from glorifying Allah, day and night.
Leaving a gathering, say: subḥānaka Allāhumma wa bi-ḥamdik.
sections.hook: Kayd returns: they plot (kaydā, 42), and their plot fails (kayduhum, 46). Sabbiḥ twice closes the surah (48, 49), ending on an-nujūm, “the stars”; the next surah opens wa-n-najm.

groups.text: By Mount Ṭūr, and by a Book written on open parchment.
By the Frequented House, the raised roof of the sky, and the sea set ablaze.
Your Lord’s punishment will certainly happen. Nothing can push it back.
On that Day the sky sways and heaves, and the mountains move away.
Woe that Day to the deniers, who spent their lives playing in falsehood.
They are shoved into Hell and told: this is the Fire you used to deny.
Is this magic, or can you not see? Burn in it; patience or panic, it’s the same.
The righteous are in gardens, delighted with their Lord’s gifts, and He saved them from the Fire.
Eat and drink happily for what you did. They recline on couches in rows, married to ḥūr ʿīn.
Believing children are raised to their parents’ rank, with no loss to anyone. Each person is pledged to his deeds.
Fruit and meat as they wish, a cup with no idle or sinful talk, and servants like hidden pearls.
They ask one another and recall: we feared Allah among our families and called on Him, and He saved us.
Keep reminding; you are no soothsayer or madman. They call you a poet and await your death; say: wait, I wait too.
Is it their minds or their rebellion? They say he made it up; then let them produce a speech like it.
Were they created by nothing, or are they their own creators? Did they create the heavens and earth? They lack certainty.
Do they own your Lord’s treasures or control things? Do they have a ladder to listen in? Then bring proof.
Does Allah have daughters while you have sons? Does the Prophet ﷺ ask them for a fee that burdens them?
Do they know the unseen, or plan a plot that will backfire? Do they have a god besides Allah? Glory be to Him.
If a piece of the sky fell on them, they’d call it piled-up clouds. So leave them until their Day of being struck down.
Their plots won’t help them then. The wrongdoers also face punishment before that, but most don’t know.
Be patient; you are under Our eyes. Glorify your Lord when you rise, in the night, and as the stars fade.

1.explain: Ṭūr: a mountain with trees, here the mountain where Allah spoke to Mūsā and revealed His rulings to him. Allah swears by it to honour it.

2.explain: Kitāb masṭūr: a written Book. Either the Preserved Tablet, a revealed scripture (the Torah or the Qurʾān), or each person’s record of deeds.

3.explain: Raqq: fine parchment for writing. Manshūr: spread open, clear to see. In one view, it is the record of deeds handed out open on the Last Day.

4.explain: Al-bayt al-maʿmūr: the angels’ Kaʿbah above the seventh heaven, in line with the Kaʿbah on earth. Seventy thousand angels enter it daily and never return. Or it means the Kaʿbah itself.

5.explain: As-saqf al-marfūʿ: the raised roof, meaning the sky. It shelters creation, and from it Allah sends rain and provision.

6.explain: Al-baḥr al-masjūr: either the sea that will be kindled into fire on the Last Day, or the sea kept full and held back from flooding the land.

7.explain: This is what the oaths were for. Your Lord’s punishment will surely land on those who deserve it. Allah never breaks His promise.

8.explain: Mā lahū min dāfiʿ: nothing can push it away or block it. No power can overcome Allah’s, and no one can run from it.

9.explain: Tamūru mawrā: the sky heaves, spins and shakes, like a turning millstone or a ship tipping over. The word gathers all these meanings.

10.explain: Tasīru sayrā: the mountains leave their places, drift like clouds, and end up as scattered dust. If they are shaken so, imagine a weak human.

11.explain: Wayl: a word for every kind of misery, fear and punishment. It is for those who denied the messengers.

12.explain: Fī khawḍin yalʿabūn: plunging into falsehood and playing. They made the religion a joke and filled their lives with distraction.

13.explain: Yudaʿʿūna daʿʿā: shoved hard, with force and roughness. They are driven to the Fire and pushed toward it on their faces.

14.explain: The keepers of Hell rebuke them: this is the very Fire you called a lie in the world.

15.explain: They called the Prophet ﷺ’s message magic. Now they are asked: is this magic too, or were you blind? Neither: the proof had reached them and was clear.

16.explain: Iṣlawhā: enter it and let it surround you. Ṣabr does nothing here: endure or panic, the pain doesn’t ease. It is only the result of what you did.

17.explain: Al-muttaqūn: those who guarded against Allah’s anger by obeying Him and avoiding what He forbade. They are in gardens and naʿīm, delight of heart, soul and body.

18.explain: Fākihīn: enjoying and delighted with their Lord’s gifts. Being saved from the Fire is a gift in itself, on top of Paradise.

19.explain: They are told: eat and drink hanīʾan, with pure joy and no ill effects. This is because of what you used to do.

20.explain: They recline at ease on couches set side by side, facing each other in good company. They are married to ḥūr ʿīn, women with large, beautiful eyes.

21.explain: Believing children are raised to their parents’ rank, even with fewer deeds, to delight the parents, who lose nothing. Rahīn: each is held by his own deeds, so no one bears another’s sins.

22.explain: Amdadnāhum: We keep supplying them, time after time, with fruit and meat, whatever they desire, even before they ask.

23.explain: Yatanāzaʿūna kaʾsā: they pass a cup to one another. Unlike worldly wine, it brings no laghw (idle talk), no taʾthīm (sinful talk), no headache and no drunkenness.

24.explain: Ghilmān: young servants going round to serve them, as beautiful as luʾluʾ maknūn, pearls kept hidden in their shells, untouched.

25.explain: They turn to one another and talk about their life in the world, what they went through, and how they reached this, out of joy and gratitude.

26.explain: Mushfiqīn: fearful. Living among our families in the world, we feared Allah’s punishment, and so kept away from sins.

27.explain: So Allah favoured us with guidance and forgiveness, and saved us from ʿadhāb as-samūm: the scorching Fire whose heat gets into the pores.

28.explain: Nadʿūhu: we used to call on Him and worship Him alone, asking Him to save us. Al-Barr: the Kind, true to His promise. Ar-Raḥīm: vast in mercy.

29.explain: Fa-dhakkir: keep reminding, and don’t stop because of their insults. Kāhin: a fortune-teller who claims news from the jinn. Majnūn: possessed or insane. By Allah’s favour, he is neither.
29.why: Reportedly revealed about the men who split up the routes into Makkah and accused the Prophet ﷺ of soothsaying, magic, madness and poetry.

30.explain: Shāʿir: a poet. Rayb al-manūn: the blows of time, or death. They hoped he would simply die like poets before him, and his message would fade.
30.why: Reportedly, when the Quraysh met in Dār an-Nadwah, one said: “Chain him and wait. He’ll die like the poets Zuhayr and an-Nābighah.” This ayah answered that.

31.explain: Tarabbaṣū: wait, then. I am waiting too: you for my death, I for Allah’s punishment on you. Reportedly it struck them at Badr.

32.explain: Aḥlām: minds. The Quraysh chiefs were famed for their intellect. Is this what their minds tell them, calling the wisest man mad? No: they are ṭāghūn, rebels without limit.

33.explain: Taqawwalahu: he made it up, a word used only for lies. The real reason they say it: bal lā yuʾminūn, they refuse to believe out of arrogance.

34.explain: Ḥadīth mithlihi: a speech like it. If they are truthful, let them, the most eloquent Arabs, produce something like the Qurʾān. They never could.

35.explain: Min ghayri shayʾ: made by nothing, with no Creator? Or did they create themselves? Both are impossible, so they must have a Creator: Allah, who alone deserves worship.

36.explain: Did they create the heavens and earth, making them Allah’s partners? Clearly not. Bal lā yūqinūn: they just lack firm certainty, or they would believe.

37.explain: Khazāʾin: treasures of provision, rain, mercy and prophethood. Do they hold them, giving and withholding as they like? Al-muṣayṭirūn: are they the ones in control? No, they are helpless.
37.why: The Makkans asked why Muḥammad ﷺ was chosen and not one of their chiefs. This answers them: choosing prophets belongs to Allah alone.

38.explain: Sullam: a ladder to heaven, where they could overhear the angels and learn their religion is true. If they claim that, let their listener bring clear proof.

39.explain: They called the angels Allah’s daughters, while they wanted sons for themselves and hated having daughters. So they gave Allah what they disliked for themselves.

40.explain: Ajr: a fee. Does the Prophet ﷺ charge them for his message, loading them with debt so they turn away? No, he asks nothing.

41.explain: Do they have the Preserved Tablet, or knowledge of the unseen to write from? Do they know the Prophet ﷺ will die before them? No one knows the unseen but Allah.

42.explain: Kayd: a plot, reportedly the plan at Dār an-Nadwah to kill him. Al-makīdūn: the plot turns on them. Allah protected him, and they were killed at Badr.

43.explain: Is there another god who provides for them or helps them? Subḥān Allāh: He is far above every partner they set up. Every question before this points here.

44.explain: Kisf: a piece. If a chunk of the sky fell on them as punishment, they would say: saḥāb markūm, just clouds heaped up. No sign moves them.
44.why: It answers their demand: “Make a piece of the sky fall on us” (26:187, see also 17:92).

45.explain: Fa-dharhum: leave them. Wait for their Day when yuṣʿaqūn: they are struck down, faint or die. That is the Day of Resurrection, or their death.

46.explain: On that Day their plotting helps them nothing, little or much. Whatever schemes worked for a while in this world fall apart, and no one saves them.

47.explain: Before the Hereafter’s punishment, the wrongdoers taste punishment now: killing at Badr, seven years of famine, or the punishment of the grave. Most don’t understand why it comes.

48.explain: Be patient with your Lord’s decision. Bi-aʿyuninā: We see you and protect you. Glorify Him with praise when you stand: rising from sleep, starting prayer, or leaving a gathering.

49.explain: Glorify Him at night too: Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ and night prayer. Idbār an-nujūm: as the stars fade, meaning the two sunnah rakʿahs before Fajr, or Fajr itself.
